about: What a test, build, typecheck or lint runner prints when it passed or failed, read from a shell call's output when its exit status can't speak for the check (a pipe into tail, `|| true`, a redirect then tail). Read by the Rust receipts (src-tauri/src/evidence.rs `read_output`, through include_str!) and meant for a JS reader too.

Each runner: `kinds` are the check kinds its failure text applies to (test, typecheck, lint, build, check, gate); `passKinds` the kinds a package script's check (`npm test`) may pass by its pass text (default: `kinds`); `fail` and `pass` are regular expressions. Runner ids and kinds never share a name.
Text: strip ANSI escapes (\u001b[...letter), then add a newline at both ends, so a pattern can take a whole line (`\n\s*2 failed\r?\n`) without anchors.

Reading one check: a runner invoked directly (`npx vitest`, `cargo test`, `node --test`, `npx playwright test`, `tsc`, `eslint`, `vite build`, `tauri build`, `cargo build|check|clippy`) is read by its own entry only: its `fail` fails it, its `pass` passes it. `npm run gate` is read by `gate-record`'s pass and every gate-kind runner's fail. Another package script: any runner of its kind (fail by `kinds`, pass by `passKinds`). Failure text always wins; only positive pass text gives `passed`.

Pass text counts only when the check is the command's only check of its kind (a package script's: its only check at all), its stdout reaches the result through tail, tee or cat only (or goes with `>`, never `>>`, to a file that every later command is a tail or cat of), and its stderr reaches the result too (`2>&1` or left alone, never `2>file` or `2>/dev/null`): anything else can drop a failure line and keep a pass line. A call that errored passes a check on text only when its exit status was the check's.

`notAfterPass`: a runner's pass text counts only when none of these come after the last pass line (cargo prints `test result: ok.` once per test binary, so an `ok.` followed by the next binary's `Running` is a run cut short). `truncated` (top level): output that holds one of these was cut or timed out, so no check passes on its text; failure text still fails.
Syntax: one pattern means the same in JS (`new RegExp(p)`, no flags) and in Rust's `regex` crate: no lookaround, no backreferences, no inline flags, no ^ or $ anchors; case-sensitive.

runners.about: Vitest's summary (`Test Files  1 failed | 3 passed (4)`, `Tests  2 failed | 8 passed (10)`) and Jest's (`Test Suites: 1 failed, 2 passed`). It passes only on the file/suite line whose first count is passed, so no file failed: `Tests  10 passed` alone may be all a `tail -3` left of a failing run. A coverage threshold miss prints after the summary (Vitest's `does not meet global threshold`, Jest's `coverage threshold for lines (90%) not met`) and fails it.

cargo test: each test binary's `test result:` line, and a build that never got to run. cargo stops at the first failing binary and ends with `error: test failed` (`error: doctest failed` for the doc tests, `error: N targets failed` with --no-fail-fast). `test result: ok.` prints once per binary, so it passes only when no later binary started after it (`notAfterPass`).
cargo build, check and clippy: `Finished` only once every crate compiled.
tauri build: cargo's `Finished … target(s)` comes before bundling, so only the bundler's own `Finished N bundle(s) at` passes it.
TypeScript: an `error TS…` line or a non-zero `Found N errors`. A clean `tsc --noEmit` prints nothing, so only watch/build mode's `Found 0 errors` passes.
node --test: the spec reporter's `ℹ pass 10` / `ℹ fail 1` and the TAP reporter's `# pass 10` / `# fail 1`.

Playwright's list reporter: a `  2 failed` (or `interrupted`) line of its own. It never passes on text: it prints `10 passed (30.2s)` last, after the failed count and the failing tests, so a `tail -1` keeps only the pass line.
ESLint's `✖ 3 problems (2 errors, 1 warning)`; a clean run prints nothing, so it never passes on text.

A package manager's own report that a script failed: npm's (`npm ERR!` / `npm error`, npm 7-11 wording), pnpm's ` ELIFECYCLE  Test failed.`, yarn's `error Command failed with exit code 1.` and bun's `error: script "test" exited with code 1`. A script that runs vitest then playwright can print vitest's pass summary before playwright fails; this line comes last.
fail: error Command failed with exit code
